title: Every backend feature has its own AJAX controller
today: Each controller parses arguments, validates them and formats errors in its own way.
solution: One generic dispatcher. Arguments and results are validated against a schema derived from the method signature.

title: No general-purpose API in the core
today: Integrations depend on extensions that each build and maintain their own endpoints.
solution: Every action is an HTTP endpoint below `/typo3/api/`, provided by TYPO3 and extensions alike.

title: Authorization is reinvented per integration
today: API keys, OAuth and fine-grained permissions are built again for every connection.
solution: EXT:hub offers OAuth 2.0 and static tokens. Scopes limit apps; the user's permissions always apply.

title: No machine-readable description
today: Endpoints are documented by hand, if at all, and the documentation drifts from the code.
solution: An OpenAPI 3.1 document is generated from the code and browsable in Swagger UI.

title: AI agents cannot work with TYPO3
today: There is no safe, standard way for assistants to read or change content on behalf of an editor.
solution: A built-in MCP server offers actions as tools. Agents act as the user, limited by the granted scopes.

title: The same logic is wrapped again for every consumer
today: Backend UI, integrations and automation each need their own glue code.
solution: Write the feature once. Every channel is available automatically.
